properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Ed25519 signature capability shipped in the solana-verify binary via the Solana keypair/signature stack. The app exercises it live: src/solana_program.rs:265 signs verification-upload transactions with a keypair loaded from the user's CLI keypair file (reported separately as a call-site finding). The signature scheme itself is fixed by the Solana protocol — replaceable only by a protocol-level migration, not unilaterally by this repo.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Curve25519 group operations (X25519/Ed25519) available to the shipped CLI binary and the Solana verification workflow. Same crate@version is also pinned in examples/hello_world_anchor/Cargo.lock:537 (reported as a separate finding for that build graph).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ring 0.17.14 supplies the classical crypto primitives (X25519 KEX, AES-GCM, SHA-2, Ed25519, ChaCha20-Poly1305) for the TLS layer of every HTTPS connection this tool makes (remote verifier + Solana RPC). Harvest-now-decrypt-later applies to the classical half; the rustls 0.23.41 sessions it serves prefer the X25519MLKEM768 hybrid by default, so the practical fix is provider/config maintenance here, not a rewrite.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: HMAC-SHA256/512 capability in the shipped binary, used for Solana seed-phrase derivation and BIP32 HD key derivation. Quantum-safe MAC — no migration pressure; note for CNSA 2.0 shops: HMAC-SHA-384 is the compliant variant.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Password-based KDF used for Solana seed-phrase derivation. The iteration count and salt handling live inside solana-seed-phrase/tiny-bip39, not in this repo, so any PBKDF2 weakness is a vendor-side issue — observable here, changeable only upstream or by replacing the derivation path. Quantum-safe (Grover square-root only).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: First-party Python crypto use: hashlib.sha256(resp.content).hexdigest() computes the digest of the Solana install script fetched over HTTPS; the digest is baked into generated Dockerfiles as INSTALL_SHA256_PLACEHOLDER and enforced at image-build time with `test "$ACTUAL" = ...` (a shell string compare of digests — same non-constant-time class as ALG-99c6681d, in generated artifacts). Supply-chain integrity pinning. Quantum-safe hash; migration to SHA-384 is low priority. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: sha2 0.10.9 (RustCrypto) in Cargo.lock:2651 — transitive dependency. Notably it is also the implementation behind the first-party hashing: the direct `sha256` crate v1.6.0 (Cargo.lock:2668) wraps sha2, and first-party code calls sha256::digest(&buffer[..]) at src/main.rs:777 for the executable-vs-on-chain hash comparison. Dependency-inventory entry — the SHA-2 implementation that ships in the binary. Changeable via Cargo.toml.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: BLAKE3-256 hashing available to the hello_world example build — the fixture program solana-verify compiles to prove deterministic builds; its lockfile is part of the repo the verifier consumes. Quantum-safe hash; no PQ action.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ring 0.17.14 (Cargo.lock:2313) provides AES-GCM record protection (plus ChaCha20-Poly1305, X25519, SHA-2) for the rustls TLS stack that carries all Rust HTTPS sessions (Solana RPC via solana-rpc-client, remote verify service via reqwest). No direct first-party call sites; the algorithms ship via the TLS layer. Note rustls 0.23.41 in this build also carries the aws-lc-rs provider — both are in the lock. Presence is the inventory fact; changeable via Cargo.

Traffic is public image metadata; the only credential in play (GITHUB_TOKEN) is read from the environment, not hardcoded.
